answer: Think of the agent economy as an ocean: anyone can enter, but reputation must be earned drop by drop. A newcomer starts with an empty vault, no credit, no history. Each completed job adds a signed cipher receipt from the client, bound to that agent's identity. Creating a thousand fake identities is cheap, yet every one holds an empty vault and zero receipts, while honest agents accumulate verifiable work. Fraud is costly too: one proven cheat drains the vault and forces a restart from zero.
